title: Integral open direct image preserves constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, and residue field $\mathbf F_E=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes in this setting [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On their small pro-étale sites use the completed coefficient sheaves $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$ and the constant finite sheaves $\mathbf F_{E,T}$, for $T=U,X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Use the derived module direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], bounded constructible categories [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, sk-def-sfb-constructible], and their finite Tor amplitude subcategories [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. If $K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$, then $Rj_*K$ is derived complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], the canonical finite-reduction comparison is an isomorphism
$$
(Rj_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}\mathbf F_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,U}}\mathbf F_{E,U}),
$$
and $Rj_*K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)=\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\pi_E$, and $P_n=A/t^nA$. Apply [sk-lem-integral-models] (2) on $U$: since $K\in\Dbc(U,A)$, $K$ is derived complete and $\bar K=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_U}(P_1)_U$ is bounded constructible and pulled back from $U_{\mathrm{ét}}$. The coefficient and scheme hypotheses are exactly its separated finite-type setting. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian (every ideal has one generator), and $P_1$ is a finite field. Its characteristic is $\ell$: the extending absolute value gives $|\ell|_E<1$, so $\ell$ lies in the maximal ideal; the residue field is nonzero and $\ell$ is prime. Thus $\ell P_1=0$, and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$.

source.place: Constructibility of the reduction, first sentence; integral criterion applied to the input

proof.text:
The coefficient resolution of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution], applied on $U$ and $X$, identifies reduction modulo $t^n$ with the cone of multiplication by $t^n$. The unbounded right derived functor $Rj_*$ is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]; its K-injective module construction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] is $A$-linear, since termwise direct image sends $t^n\operatorname{id}$ to $t^n\operatorname{id}$. It therefore sends the reduction cone of $K$ to the reduction cone of $Rj_*K$. To fix the canonical comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of cones, apply the finite-reduction clause of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] with $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(t))$ and $f=j$. The tower datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] requires every $P_n$ to be finite and perfect over $A$; these exact hypotheses are supplied, for all $n\ge1$, by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. Its two-term finite free resolution is the ring-module counterpart of the sheaf resolution above. The residue is torsion by step 1, and $I$ has the single generator $t$. It identifies the projection-formula comparison
$$(Rj_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}(P_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_U}(P_n)_U)$$
and states that it commutes with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$. The case $n=1$ is the comparison asserted in the item. All categories here use completed coefficient sheaves, as in that node's tower datum; no identification with discrete constant $A$-module categories is made.

source.place: Reduction paragraph; use all powers t^n and the canonical compatible comparisons

proof.text:
Let $K_\bullet$ be the reduction tower of $K$. The canonical completion unit $K\to R\varprojlim K_\bullet$ is an isomorphism by step 1 and [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Apply the derived-limit comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]: it gives
$$Rj_*K\simeq Rj_*R\varprojlim K_\bullet\simeq R\varprojlim Rj_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet.$$
Its evaluation identifications identify the level $n$ of the last tower with $Rj_*K_n$. By the compatible canonical reduction isomorphisms of step 2, these are exactly the reductions of $Rj_*K$, including their transition maps. The completion-map clause of the cited node identifies this composite with the canonical completion unit of $Rj_*K$, not just an abstract isomorphism with some inverse limit. Hence $Rj_*K$ is derived complete.

source.place: Completeness paragraph; include identification of the tower and its completion map

proof.text: The constructible comparison [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] applies to the finite discrete field $P_1$ and the qcqs scheme $U$. It supplies $L\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{ét}},P_1)$ with $\nu_U^*L\simeq\bar K$. Apply [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients] with $A=P_1$ and annihilating integer $\ell$: $U,X$ are finite-type over $k$, $j$ is open, $P_1$ is finite, and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$ by step 1. Consequently $Rj_{\mathrm{ét},*}L\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},P_1)$. This is the finite-coefficient open-finiteness input of the blueprint; no properness of $j$ is required.

source.place: Constructibility of the reduction; descend the complex and apply finite-coefficient open finiteness

proof.text: The open immersion $j$ is quasi-separated: $U\times_XU\cong U$ and its diagonal is the identity, whose inverse image of an affine open is that affine open and hence quasi-compact. Together with the assumed quasi-compactness, this makes $j$ qcqs. This uses only the open-immersion and quasi-compactness definitions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: check the qcqs hypothesis

proof.text:
Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $j$ and the bounded-below complex $L$ of step 4. Its natural comparison and $\nu_U^*L\simeq\bar K$ give
$$Rj_{B,*}\bar K\simeq\nu_X^*Rj_{\mathrm{ét},*}L,\qquad B_T=(P_1)_T.$$
By step 4 and the bounded constructible equivalence [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] on $X$, this is a bounded constructible $B_X$-complex of étale origin. Here $Rj_{B,*}$ denotes direct image with the residue coefficient rings, before restriction to $A_X$-modules.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: apply qcqs comparison at residue coefficients

proof.text:
For $T=U,X$ let $a_T:A_T\to B_T$ be reduction, the pullback from the point of $\underline{\mathcal O_E}\to\underline{P_1}$. Apply [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] to these two coefficient rings: it supplies the ring isomorphisms $c_A:j^{-1}A_X\simeq A_U$ and $c_B:j^{-1}B_X\simeq B_U$. The coefficient-change square of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] states exactly $a_Uc_A=c_Bj^{-1}a_X$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] applies with $u=j$, $R_T=A_T$, $S_T=B_T$. Its direct-image comparison, inverted, gives
$$Rj_{A,*}\operatorname{Res}_U\bar K\simeq\operatorname{Res}_X Rj_{B,*}\bar K.$$
This cited lemma treats arbitrary compatible ring sheaves; it requires neither finite $A$ nor flatness of $B_T$ over $A_T$.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: coefficient square and derived scalar-restriction comparison

proof.text: Put $M=(Rj_{A,*}K)\otimes^L_{A_X}B_X$ and $N=Rj_{B,*}\bar K$. The case $n=1$ of step 2, followed by step 7, gives $\operatorname{Res}_X M\simeq\operatorname{Res}_X N$ in $D(A_X)$. Restriction along $A_X\to B_X$ is exact by [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], so its cohomology is the restriction of the $B_X$-cohomology. Consequently these isomorphisms induce $A_X$-linear isomorphisms $H^q(M)\simeq H^q(N)$ for every $q$.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: compare cohomology after exact restriction

proof.text: The quotient $A_X\to B_X$ is an epimorphism by the exact coefficient resolution of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] with $n=1$, already used in step 2. Each section $b$ of $B_X$ therefore lifts locally to a section $a$ of $A_X$. For an $A_X$-linear map $h:H^q(M)\to H^q(N)$ from step 8 and a local section $m$, one has $h(bm)=h(am)=a h(m)=b h(m)$ on such a cover; the sheaf condition gives the equality globally. The same computation applies to the inverse. Thus $H^q(M)\simeq H^q(N)$ as $B_X$-modules. Step 6 now implies that $M$ is bounded with constructible residue-coefficient cohomology.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: elementary descent of linearity along the coefficient epimorphism

proof.text: The discrete field $P_1$ is Noetherian, and $X$ is qcqs in the standing setting. Hence the derived equivalence of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] applies to the bounded constructible $B_X$-complex $M$ of step 9. In particular $M$ is pulled back from a bounded constructible complex on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$. This verifies the étale-origin condition for the actual residue reduction of $Rj_{A,*}K$, without lifting the ambient $A_X$-derived isomorphism of step 8 to a morphism of $B_X$-complexes.

source.place: Constructibility paragraph: deduce étale origin for the actual residue reduction

proof.text: Steps 3 and 10 establish the two conditions in [sk-lem-integral-models] (2) on $X$: derived completeness and bounded constructible étale-origin residue reduction. It follows that $Rj_*K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. The same node explicitly asserts $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)=\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$ in this setting, so the finite Tor amplitude conclusion also follows. This uses the existing residue criterion, which realizes the blueprint's reference to the integral constructibility criterion, and proves every clause of the item.

source.place: Conclusion paragraph, including the finite Tor amplitude equality

proof_origin.place: All four paragraphs, expanded in eleven steps; general coefficient-change and exact restriction lemmas replace the hidden argument in former step 5

split_report.summary: Repair of the 2026-10-17 re-split request: retain the statement, Lean record, proof route and original steps 1-4 and conclusion. Replace former step 5 by short steps citing the existing general ring-sheaf change-of-coefficients comparison, Cartesian coefficients, the coefficient-change square, and exact restriction. Write quotient-linearity as its own elementary section calculation and use constructible comparison to recover etale origin. No new nodes: the needed non-elementary lemmas already exist.
split_report.blueprint: Completeness paragraph: steps 1 and 3; Reduction: step 2; Constructibility of the reduction: steps 4-10; Conclusion: step 11. The original statement and all four parts of its route are preserved.

Verify the finite perfect quotient hypotheses of the direct-image tower tool.

Use exact scalar restriction from residue to completed coefficients to identify cohomology, a generic coefficient tool.
